rule: An s x s block of 0 slides through the non-wall (non-3) cells. If it can reach the s x s block of 2, it replaces it. Otherwise it stops at the unique reachable top-left position farthest from its start in slide steps. The cells it vacates become 1.
scope: Square blocks of side 1..4 slide in tree corridors or widened rectangular/staircase rooms with optional extra connections. Exact width/height controls up to 30 are honored. Random dimensions must be at least 3*size+4. Reachable goals and uniquely farthest unreachable destinations are independently checked after geometry construction. Explicit canonical wall layouts preserve fixture reconstruction.

authored_scope: Random scenes are trees of exactly-s-wide tubes on an irregular lattice. Pitch is at least s+1 and grids are at most 30x30. Block size is 1..4. The mover and goal sit at distinct leaves, optionally flush against the grid edge. Narrow dead-end spurs (width < s) serve as distractors. In the unreachable case (s >= 2 only), one edge on the start-to-goal path is narrowed below s. Not supported: open rooms wider than the block, corridors with cycles, and diagonal or irregular wall shapes like those in some fixtures. Fixtures are replayed from explicit wall layouts plus size, start and goal.
authored_constraints: Mover and goal are equal s x s squares on fully open cells and do not overlap.
Non-incident tubes are separated by at least one wall cell, so the block-position graph is a subdivided tree.
Spurs and narrow strips are narrower than s, never share a lattice gap with another tube, and add no new block positions.
Unreachable scenes have a unique farthest reachable position; ties are rejected and resampled.
The destination always differs from the start, so no identity samples occur.
s = 1 scenes are always reachable, because a narrower-than-1 passage is impossible.
The search tie-break (direction order down, up, right, left) matches the specification but is never needed in random scenes.
